## Drivers

The drivers $u_1, \dots, u_4$ (`TT`, `DL`, `RAW`, `RAD`) are standardised to mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The response does not enter this step.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("make_drivers")
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: 03-1
#| ref.label: 03-1-run
#| eval: false
```

## Python

```python
drv = make_drivers(wx)
print(drv.U.shape)           # season x day x driver
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 03-1-run
#| echo: false
drv <- make_drivers(wx)
dim(drv$U)            # season x day x driver
```

## Library

The library contains powers of each driver up to degree 3, giving $K = 12$ terms; the constant term is the intercept of the regression.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("library_matrix", "make_library")
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: 03-2
#| ref.label: 03-2-run
#| eval: false
```

## Python

```python
Theta = make_library(drv)
print(Theta.array.shape)     # season x day x term
print(Theta.terms)
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 03-2-run
#| echo: false
Theta <- make_library(drv)
dim(Theta)            # season x day x term
dimnames(Theta)[[3]]
```

## Design matrix

For one genotype, the rows of $\mathbf{X}$ are the days of all seasons and the columns are the library terms; $\Delta\mathbf{y}$ holds the daily biomass increments $y_{i+1} - y_i$.

![The regression problem for genotype `g114` (first 30 rows shown; entries of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\Delta\mathbf{y}$ standardised, coloured from negative (red) to positive (blue)). The coefficient vector $\boldsymbol{\xi}$ is sparse: grey cells are removed terms.](images/concept_design.png){width=100%}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("make_design")
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: 03-4
#| ref.label: 03-4-run
#| eval: false
```

## Python

```python
d = make_design(Theta, tr, "g001")
print(d.X.shape)
print(d.X[:3].round(2))
print(d.dy[:6])
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 03-4-run
#| echo: false
d <- make_design(Theta, tr, "g001")
dim(d$X)
round(head(d$X, 3), 2)
head(d$dy)
```

The regression of the increments on the library is a linear model:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: 03-5

```

## Python

```python
print(pd.Series(fit_ols(d.X, d.dy), index=["1"] + d.terms).round(3))
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 03-5-run
#| echo: false
round(coef(lm(d$dy ~ d$X)), 3)
```

Step 4 replaces `lm` by other methods.
